channel.description: Noticias globales de insurtech, actualizadas cada 6 horas.

item.title: Humans, Not AI, Still A Cause of Most Cyber Losses in First Half of Year
item.description: More than 85% of incurred cyber losses in the first half of 2026 were from attacks that exploited human error, specifically where the point of failure included phishing, social engineering, or transfer fraud, according to a report out on Thursday from cyber insurer Resilience. They were up from 17.7% of incurred losses in the first half of 2024 to 85.3% in the same period this year, marking the single largest increase among loss drivers over the five half-year periods. Humans, not artificial intelligence threats, are the cause of the large majority of cyber-attacks — for now.

item.title: The Impact of Subsidization on Commercial Auto Telematics Programs
item.description: For quite some time now, commercial auto carriers have debated the notion that there is an inverse relationship between the subsidization of telematics program costs and program performance. The idea is that if the insured is not paying for their telematics solution, then they have no skin in the game and will not invest as much discipline into the program as those that pay for their solution. This is the old adage about people not valuing things that they didn’t pay for.

item.title: Fitch Warns AI Market Correction Emerging as Major Global Credit Risk
item.description: The AI boom and the risk of a correction are emerging as major global credit risks, ratings agency Fitch has warned, adding to growing concerns that soaring tech valuations and unprecedented AI spending may be running ahead of uncertain future returns. In its third-quarter Global Risk Outlook, Fitch said the credit backdrop remains dominated by two short-term risks: mounting vulnerability to an AI-related market correction and continued uncertainty linked to the U.S.-Iran conflict. “The scale of AI investment is such that the exposure of the economy and overall capital market to such a correction is significant,” Fitch said.

item.title: FCA censures Equity for Growth (Securities) Limited
item.description: The FCA has censured Equity for Growth (Securities) Limited (EFG) for approving financial promotions relating to minibonds that were unfair, unclear and misleading. EFG approved financial promotions which failed to disclose very high commission fees charged by its appointed representatives and other introducers for marketing the minibonds to investors. Appointed representatives carry out regulated activities under the responsibility of an authorised firm, known as ‘the principal’.

item.title: Founder Traits And One Big AI Test: How Former NEA Partner Vanessa Larco Picks Winners
item.description: In early 2025, Vanessa Larco teamed up with Mercedes Bent to found Premise VC , a firm focused on backing early-stage technical founders building durable, high-growth software. Before that, Larco had spent nearly eight years as a partner at New Enterprise Associates (NEA), one of the world’s largest venture capital firms. Crunchbase News recently sat down with Larco to discuss how changing founder preferences and the Silicon Valley Bank (SVB) collapse drove her to launch a specialized pre-seed and seed fund designed to make early-stage founders a top priority.

item.title: Mt. Logan grows total AUM to $3.4bn, helped by Everest’s Annapurna sidecar
item.description: Logan Capital Management platform with the launch of the market’s largest casualty and specialty sidecar, Annapurna Re.” On the casualty sidecar, Everest noted that it, “Provides additional capital flexibility and is expected to be modestly accretive to underwriting income and ROE over time.” On a quarterly basis, Everest expects to cede around $200 million of premiums to the Annapurna Re sidecar structure, the company said. (MLCM), the Everest Group owned third-party capital management platform, has expanded its assets under management meaningfully over recent months, reaching $3.4 billion in AUM, helped by parent Everest’s launch of what was the largest casualty reinsurance sidecar to be launched in the market. Since that April AUM figure, Everest launched Annapurna Re Ltd., which is the specialty re/insurers first casualty reinsurance sidecar .

item.title: Munich Re pegs global insured catastrophe losses at $44bn for H1 2026
item.description: Reinsurance firm Munich Re has estimated that global insured losses from natural catastrophe events reached US $44 billion in the first-half of 2026, below long-term averages, and a notable decline from last year’s $80 billion. Munich Re’s data on global insured natural catastrophe losses of $44 billion for H1 2026 compares to broker Aon’s estimate of at least $47 billion, and reinsurance broker Gallagher Re’s estimate of $46 billion. The United States dominated global insured catastrophe losses again, causing total economic losses of around $47 billion by June, $34 billion of which were insured.

item.title: Artemis London 2026: Four new expert speakers and Early Bird rate ends tomorrow
item.description: We have added four new expert speakers to the Artemis London 2026 website. We are delighted to add four new expert speakers to the conference roster for Artemis London 2026, adding to the deep sector expertise across our speaker faculty Speaking on the day at the conference will be: Our agenda for the conference will be revealed next week and we may have a few more speakers to reveal over the coming weeks as well. Early Bird tickets are very limited in number and this rate will end after tomorrow.

item.title: Markel Insurance’s underwriting profit more than doubles to $142m in Q2’26
item.description: Underwriting profit for the core specialty insurance division more than doubled to $142.1 million in Q2 2026, up from $63.2 million in the same period of 2025. Tom Gayner, Chief Executive Officer of Markel, commented, “In the first half of 2026, our insurance underwriting improved, our businesses generated strong cash flow, and we continued to allocate capital with discipline, including ongoing share repurchases funded from net earnings. Markel Insurance delivered a 40% surge in adjusted operating income to $376.5 million for Q2 2026, serving as the primary growth engine for Markel Group.

item.title: The Baldwin Group says softer property market offers opportunities despite ongoing casualty pressures
item.description: The Baldwin Group, a US independent insurance brokerage and advisory company, has reported that commercial property insurance continues to become more affordable, although businesses should remain cautious as liability-related risks continue to place pressure on casualty insurance markets. In its Q2 2026 Market Pulse Report, The Baldwin Group said commercial property insurance pricing fell by 8.1% during the second quarter, extending a run of declines that has now lasted five consecutive quarters. “Property and casualty are creating two very different renewal conversations,” commented Leslie Nylund, National Managing Director of Broking and Insurance Company Partnerships at The Baldwin Group.

item.title: Insured losses from nat cats reached $44bn in H1’26: Munich Re
item.description: Munich Re, a global reinsurer and provider of primary insurance and risk solutions, has disclosed that in the first half of 2026, insured losses from natural disasters totalled USD 44 billion, representing a 60% insurance gap, as overall global losses totalled nearly USD 112 billion. The best way for society to reduce losses is to stop building in high-risk areas and to keep investing in prevention.” According to Munich Re, the most destructive natural disaster was a double earthquake in Venezuela on 24 June, which, according to preliminary estimates, is expected to cause total losses of USD 30 billion, although insured losses of less than a billion, regionally. The reinsurer, in its new report, Lower losses, growing risks: the natural disaster review for the first half of 2026, explained that losses were slightly below the inflation-adjusted average figures for the first half of the year over the past ten years (overall losses: USD113 billion; insured losses: USD 50 billion), but significantly below the 5-year average figures (overall losses: USD 136 billion; insured losses: USD 66 billion).

item.title: Drone Strike Near Suez Canal in Egypt Raises New Security Threat in Widening War
item.description: A drone strike on gas vessels in Egypt’s Mediterranean port of Damietta signaled a potential new front in the U.S.-Iran war, raising the prospect of threats to navigation through the Suez Canal, a last remaining safe export route for Saudi oil. The Egyptian cabinet said on Thursday that an initial investigation showed that an unidentified drone caused a fire on Wednesday on two vessels at Damietta port, near the Suez Canal, which links the Mediterranean with the Red Sea. No group has claimed responsibility, the cabinet said, adding that authorities were taking measures to protect Egypt’s national security.

item.title: Japan Earthquake’s Insurance Claims May Top $1.1 Billion: Bloomberg Intelligence
item.description: Insurance claims from this week’s earthquake in Japan may top the 175 billion yen ($1.1 billion) average for the country’s six previous major tremors, Bloomberg Intelligence estimated.” We estimate industry-wide insurance claims could reach the low hundreds of billions of yen,” BI analyst Steven Lam said in a report. Most of the exposure from the July 28 quake in Kumamoto is tied to commercial properties, as well as residential coverage under Japan’s earthquake insurance system, he said. This story was produced with the assistance of Bloomberg Automation Photograph: A destroyed building is seen next to homes in Hikawa, Japan on July 30, 2026; photo credit: Philip Fong/AFP/Getty Images Topics Catastrophe Natural Disasters Claims

item.title: Houthis’ Red Sea Attacks Prompt London Insurers to Widen High-Risk Zone
item.description: Attacks on ships by Yemen’s Houthis have prompted London’s marine insurance market to widened its “high risk” zone in the Red Sea . The extended high-risk zone takes in more of the Red Sea coast adjacent to Saudi Arabian ports and reaches close to the Saudi port of Jizan, The JWC said in a July 29 advisory. “The decision …to amend those listed areas reflects the recent escalation by the Houthis and their attacks on Saudi vessels in the Red Sea,” Neil Roberts, head of marine and aviation with the LMA and the JWC secretary, said in a statement on Thursday.

item.title: Aviva appoints Emma Stewart as Chief Underwriting Officer for Personal Lines
item.description: Aviva has appointed Emma Stewart as Chief Underwriting Officer for its Personal Lines business , effective December 1, 2026 , as the insurer continues to strengthen its leadership team following the integration of Direct Line Group . In her new role, Stewart will lead Aviva’s Personal Lines Underwriting function and become a member of the Personal Lines Executive Committee. Executive comments Owen Morris, Chief Executive of UK Personal Lines at Aviva, welcomed Stewart’s appointment.

item.title: Plymouth Rock Assurance brings home insurance quoting to ChatGPT
item.description: Plymouth Rock announced the availability of home insurance quoting through ChatGPT. The new plugin enables homeowners to receive a home insurance quote within ChatGPT across all states where Plymouth Rock operates, including Massachusetts, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Connecticut, New York, and New Hampshire. Plymouth Rock delivers all the above.” – Bill Martin, President and CEO of Plymouth Rock Home Assurance.

item.title: Arch RoamRight partners with TravelJoy
item.description: Arch RoamRight, a provider of travel insurance solutions, announced a new partnership with TravelJoy, the all-in-one CRM and booking platform for travel advisors. Through this integration, advisors can quote and purchase Arch RoamRight travel insurance directly within TravelJoy. Bringing Arch RoamRight into the TravelJoy workflow lets advisors quote and add travel protection without switching tools, reentering details, or breaking their momentum.

item.title: La suscripción sigue siendo el principal caso de uso de la IA en seguros
item.description: Una encuesta de GlobalData entre profesionales del sector asegurador revela que la suscripción y el perfilado de riesgos sigue siendo el área donde se espera mayor impacto de la inteligencia artificial, citada por el 34,4% de los encuestados, aunque su peso ha caído 11,4 puntos porcentuales respecto a julio de 2025.

item.title: Insurance Europe pide que no se penalice el uso del reaseguro proporcional
item.description: El Reinsurance Advisory Board (RAB) de Insurance Europe ha reclamado a Eiopa un enfoque proporcionado en el tratamiento supervisor del reaseguro proporcional y ha advertido de que un endurecimiento excesivo de los criterios podría reducir la capacidad del mercado y encarecer la cobertura disponible para las aseguradoras europeas.

item.title: España es el cuarto país del mundo por número de mutualidades de seguros
item.description: España cuenta con alrededor de 300 mutualidades y cooperativas de seguros, lo que la sitúa como el cuarto país del mundo por número de entidades de este tipo, según el informe ‘Global Mutual Market Share 2026’ elaborado por la International Cooperative and Mutual Insurance Federation (ICMIF).

item.title: Hims & Hers Sued by FTC, Utah in Federal Court
item.description: The Federal Trade Commission, Utah and Los Angeles County sued Hims & Hers Health Inc. In a lawsuit filed in California federal court, the agency said Hims failed to disclose to consumers that they were purchasing a subscription, made it too difficult to cancel and mislead them about the privacy of their information by sharing it with the social networks for advertising purposes. The FTC said those business practices violate federal consumer protection laws, while Utah and LA alleged violations of state laws.

item.title: Goldman Sachs Must Pay Male Banker $1.9 Million for Sex Discrimination
item.description: A former Goldman Sachs senior compliance officer has been awarded £1.45 million ($1.93 million) for sex discrimination and unfair dismissal after he was fired while on parental leave, a London court has ruled. Related: Goldman Sachs Paying $500M to Settle Shareholder Suit Over 1MDB Scandal Goldman Sachs said it was a market leader in paid parental leave and encouraged all working parents – regardless of gender – to take the 26 weeks paid leave offered. Jonathan Reeves, a Goldman veteran who last worked for the bank in London, won the first part of his case two years ago after a judge found he was unfairly dismissed and discriminated against in 2022 after he took six months of parental leave under a policy offered by the bank.

item.title: X, World Federation of Advertisers Settle Litigation Over GARM Dispute
item.description: SpaceX’s X and the World Federation of Advertisers (WFA) said on Wednesday they had settled litigation over an alleged advertiser boycott of the social media platform linked to the now-defunct Global Alliance for Responsible Media (GARM). X, formerly known as Twitter, filed the lawsuit in 2024, alleging the advertisers, acting through WFA’s GARM initiative, collectively withheld billions of dollars in advertising spending from the platform due to disagreements over content moderation policies. The trade body also said it had permanently discontinued GARM in August 2024 and would not revive the initiative or create a similar program.

item.title: SCOR pulls-back on non-cat US property, flat on property cat, at “competitive” renewals
item.description: Global reinsurer SCOR said this morning it applied underwriting discipline at the “competitive” mid-year reinsurance renewals this year, growing in diversifying areas of the market, most notably in its alternative solutions business, while decreasing premiums written in non-cat US property lines, but remaining flat in US property catastrophe business. But, demonstrating cycle management, SCOR said that P&C renewal business decreased 4.8%, with particular reductions in in non-cat US property business and also US casualty business, while the company remained flat in property catastrophe business at the renewals. We have entered the second half of 2026 from a position of strength, firmly focused on delivering Forward 2026.” Commenting on market conditions, SCOR explained that the mid-year reinsurance renewals were competitive.

item.title: Nephila Capital ILS fund management revenues rise 23% in Q2, 30% for first-half 2026
item.description: Nephila Capital’s insurance-linked securities (ILS) fund management revenues reported within parent Markel’s results have risen strongly by 23% in the second-quarter of 2026 and now by 30% for the first-half of the year. For the first-half of 2026, ILS fund management revenues rose to $78.1 million, a 30% increase over H1 2025’s ILS fund revenues of $54.6 million earned by the Nephila Capital business. After the first-quarter of this year, Nephila Capital’s insurance-linked securities fund management revenues had risen by an impressive 59% year-on-year, to reach $40.5 million for Q1 2026 .

item.title: Previsico takes flood intelligence technology to Africa
item.description: UK flood intelligence specialist Previsico has announced its entry into the African market, beginning with South Africa, as part of its ongoing international expansion. Bringing Previsico to South Africa is more than a market expansion, it’s a chance to bring flood intelligence to those who need it most. Previsico’s flood intelligence equips insurers and communities in South Africa with actionable insights that were previously unavailable.” Previsico said the South African launch represents the latest stage of its international growth strategy.

item.title: SCOR reports €171m Q2’26 net income as P&C CoR improves to 79.5%
item.description: Global reinsurer SCOR reported group net income of €171 million for the second quarter of 2026, supported by strong contributions across all business lines, while its P&C combined ratio improved to 79.5% on the back of benign natural catastrophe losses, better attritional claims experience and additional reserve strengthening. According to SCOR, insurance revenue reflected the “positive” renewals outcome, partly offset by EGPI revisions on existing business and foreign exchange headwinds. SCOR attributed the increase mainly to business volumes, lower retrocession costs, and higher contributions from SBS and Cedant Facultative.

item.title: Everest posts $559m net income as GWP falls 7.1% in Q2’26
item.description: Bermuda-based re/insurer Everest Group, Ltd. recorded net income of $559 million in the second quarter of 2026, while gross written premium (GWP) from its Core businesses decreased by 7.1% year-on-year to $3.7 billion, driven by a 9.1% decrease in its Reinsurance Treaty arm. Net income of $559 million is down on last year’s $680 million, as net operating income fell to $585 million from $734 million, while pre-tax underwriting income hit $281 million for the Group.

item.title: Lemonade Posts $43M Loss for Q2 as it Continues to Grow Customer Base
item.description: Insurtech Lemonade reported a second quarter 2026 net loss of about $43 million compared with a loss of about $44 million during the same time in 2025. Lemonade said its topline growth was positive, with 76% increase in year-over-year gross profit to a record of about $113 million. Customer count increased by 23% to about 3.3 million.

item.title: Viewpoint: Who Gets Credit for Successful Renewal During Soft Reinsurance Market?
item.description: That may seem like a subtle distinction, but it raises an important question: who gets the credit for a successful renewal? One theme that has come up repeatedly in conversations with reinsurance brokers recently is that achieving a good renewal outcome is no longer always enough to demonstrate value. “In a market where renewal outcomes may increasingly look similar on paper, the brokers best positioned to defend and grow relationships are likely to be those whose clients understand not only what decision was made, but why it was made and how it was reached.” From the client’s perspective, that is not an unreasonable conclusion.

item.title: FTC Sues Hims & Hers for Sending User Health Info to Meta, Snap
item.description: Federal Trade Commission sued Hims & Hers on July 29 alleging the telehealth platform shared users’ health data with online advertisers, despite promising privacy, and engaged in deceptive billing and cancellation practices. Users’ sensitive health information was shared with online advertising companies including Meta Platforms and Snap d espite the company leading customers to believe their data was private , the FTC alleged in the lawsuit filed along with Los Angeles County and Utah. Hims & Hers stock added to losses after the news and was trading down around 12%.

item.title: Inszone Insurance Acquires Pennsylvania Hospitality Specialist Progress Brokerage
item.description: Inszone Insurance Services, a national provider of commercial, personal, and benefits insurance, announced the acquisition of Progress Brokerage Group, LLC, a specialized insurance agency based in Springfield, Pennsylvania. Founded in 2013 by Ed Snow, Progress Brokerage Group has built a reputation serving bars, restaurants, taverns, and hospitality businesses throughout Pennsylvania and neighboring markets. “Their expertise in hospitality insurance and their dedication to client service make them an outstanding addition to Inszone as we continue expanding throughout the East Coast,” said Chris Walters, CEO of California-based Inszone Insurance Services.

item.title: Utica National Teams Up With NFL’s Buffalo Bills
item.description: Utica National Insurance Group announced a partnership with the National Football League’s Buffalo Bills. “We’re proud to stand alongside the Buffalo Bills and bring Bills’ energy to everything we do” State Kristen Martin, president and CEO of Utica National. As the football season approaches, Utica National said it will roll out a series of “campaigns and engagements designed to celebrate the partnership, energize fans, and reinforce its commitment to protecting what matters most.” The insurer is planning game day activations, co-branded community initiatives, and integrated marketing campaigns.

item.title: Making AI Work in Commercial Submission Intake
item.description: The industry no longer doubts whether AI benefits submission intake in commercial property and casualty (P&C) lines. Which parts of their submission intake workflow can realistically be automated? In this article, I'll share my perspective on where AI works best in submission intake today, why many initiatives never move beyond pilots, and what insurers should focus on if they want to launch submission intake AI over the next six to 12 months.

item.title: Curant.ai raises $3.1 million
item.description: Curant.ai has raised $3.1 million in seed funding to expand its AI platform for insurance operations. Curant integrates with insurers’ existing systems and provides source-backed insights and workflows configured around each carrier’s processes. Diagram led the round, with participation from Humania Insurance, Element Ventures, Blue Plains Capital and several angel investors.

item.title: Trucordia acquires the assets of Dominion Insurance Services
item.description: Trucordia has acquired the assets of Dominion Insurance Services , a California-based boutique brokerage specializing in lawyers professional liability and other professional liability lines. Founded in 1997 by Larry Hilton, and later joined by Wes Hilton, Dominion serves law firms and other professional clients, offering coverage including lawyers professional liability, fiduciary liability, patent agent liability, and insurance for accountants, architects and engineers. The acquisition expands Trucordia’s professional liability capabilities while providing Dominion with broader resources and operational support.

item.title: Utica National partners with the Buffalo Bills
item.description: Utica National has become an official home, auto and business insurance partner of the Buffalo Bills. The partnership will feature community-focused initiatives and events across Upstate New York, including the annual Utica National Kids Run and the Thanksgiving Blitz food drive in Buffalo. Utica National will also use the relationship to increase its brand visibility and promote its network of independent insurance agents.

item.title: AFBA Launches Benekiva Claims Platform
item.description: (Image source: AFBA.) Armed Forces Benefit Association (Alexandria, Va.) has gone live with Benekiva (West Des Moines, Iowa) for life insurance member-benefit claims processing. The AI-enabled claims platform was implemented in six months and supports AFBA’s benefit payment process from initial notification to reconciliation, according to an AFBA statement. The Benekiva deployment uses streamlined workflows and integrations to reduce double entry and speed claims processing, according to AFBA.

item.title: Verisk Acquires McKenzie Intelligence Services
item.description: (Image source: McKenzie Intelligence Services.) Verisk (Jersey City, N.J.) has acquired McKenzie Intelligence Services (London), a geospatial intelligence and event-response company focused on catastrophe and conflict event analysis. MIS provides rapid post-event damage assessment and real-time intelligence for major loss events, according to a Verisk statement. The acquisition brings MIS into Verisk’s Catastrophe and Risk Solutions business, adding geospatial event intelligence to Verisk’s catastrophe models, risk analytics and claims solutions.

item.title: Florida’s Fix for Insurance Crisis Puts More Risk on Homeowners
item.description: Florida changed how the legal system applies to insurance companies, making it more onerous for homeowners to use the courts to challenge denied claims or low payouts. Florida lawmakers knew they had a billion-dollar insurance problem. Scientists say this is a consequence of climate change, and a dynamic that will accelerate; many in the insurance industry say homeowners were weaponizing natural catastrophes to file fraudulent claims.

item.title: Cost of a Data Breach Reaches Record $5 Million on Average
item.description: Artificial intelligence has “radically shifted” the cyber risk landscape, and the average cost of a data breach has reached a record of nearly $5 million. AI-driven attacks increased 56% over last year’s study, adding about $1 million to the cost of a breach reach an average $4.99 million—a 12% increase. “Three quarters said they will deploy agents at higher rates in alert triage, vulnerability management, and scans and penetration testing.” IBM said average breach costs are worse in the U.S., reaching a record of about $11.5 million thanks to traditionally higher business costs and regulatory fines.

item.title: Workplaces Dialing Down ‘Tokenmaxxing’ as Focus Returns to ROI
item.description: A corporate fad of “tokenmaxxing” artificial intelligence is hitting its limits as workplaces using AI for everything are seeing costs rise without a spike in productivity. “Tokenmaxxing” refers to maximizing usage of tokens — the building blocks of generative AI that correspond to small pieces of text that an AI system reads or writes. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said in May he was “excited to see what will happen with tokenmaxxing startups, both for how they work internally and the products they can build.” Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said, “If your $500K engineer isn’t burning $250K in tokens, something is wrong.” Facebook parent Meta had an internal competition rewarding token usage.

item.title: Cyclosporiasis Cases in Michigan Surpass 10,000 in Ongoing Outbreak
item.description: Michigan health officials reported 10,077 cases of cyclosporiasis on Wednesday, an increase of 397 cases since their last update a day earlier. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has received reports of 6,707 laboratory-confirmed domestic cases of cyclosporiasis, and said it was aware of more than 11,500 additional cases that are not laboratory confirmed or require further investigation across 45 states. Food and Drug Administration has linked the outbreak to iceberg lettuce served at Taco Bell restaurants sourced from privately held Taylor Farms operations in central Mexico, but authorities are still looking for other potential sources given the size of the outbreak.

item.title: Dealer Installed Anti-Theft System Puts More Than 2M Vehicles in California at Higher Theft Risk
item.description: Computer scientists at the University of California, San Diego, uncovered a higher risk of theft in cars with dealer-installed anti-theft systems in Southern California since 2017. Vehicles purchased at Honda, Toyota, Mazda, Ford, and Jeep dealerships in Southern California from 2017 to present, with a sticker displaying the word “KARR” or “SWDS” on the driver’s-side window, are at risk. More than 2 million cars could be vulnerable to an attack that allows thieves to lock and unlock doors from as far as five yards away and immobilize vehicle engines remotely via a Bluetooth connection, according to a press release issued last week by the university.

item.title: Tokenized reinsurance securities will lower barriers and expand market access: HCI’s Patel
item.description: In light of HCI Group’s interest in taking risk on-chain and issuing tokenized reinsurance securities through a new partnership with Oxbridge Re, Chairman and CEO Paresh Patel has highlighted how tokenized reinsurance securities have the potential to expand access to the reinsurance market by lowering investment barriers and shortening investment duration. “While still in its early stages, we believe tokenized reinsurance securities have the potential to expand access to the reinsurance market by lowering investment barriers, shortening investment duration, and creating the potential for increased liquidity for qualified investors.” Back in June, Oxbridge Re and its subsidiary, SurancePlus, partnered with HCI Group to launch three Solana-based tokenized reinsurance securities tied to HCI’s recently formed reinsurer Fortex Re.
